nodes.text: If\[n! = \prod_i p_i^{k_i}\]is the factorisation into distinct primes then let $h(n)$ count the number of distinct exponents $k_i$. Prove that there exists some $c>0$ such that\[h(n) \sim c \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}\]as $n\to \infty$.

#912 : [Er82c] number theory | factorials A problem of Erdős and Selfridge, who proved (see [Er82c] )\[h(n) \asymp \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}.\]A heuristic of Tao using the Cramér model for the primes (detailed in the comments) suggests this is true with\[c=\sqrt{2\pi}=2.506\cdots.\] Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
